lessons.title: Lesson 1: PHP Basics & Hello World
lessons.html:
Your First PHP Script

PHP is a server-side scripting language designed for web development. Runs on server, generates HTML.

Basic Structure:

  • <?php ?> - PHP tags
  • echo - Output to browser
  • ; - Statement terminator
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html>
<body>
<?php
  echo "Hello, PHP!";
  $name = "World";
  echo "<h2>Hello, $name!</h2>";
?>
</body>
</html>

Run: Save as index.php, open in browser via web server.

Practice Exercises:

  1. Modify the code example to handle edge cases
  2. Write a test case for the main functionality
  3. Refactor the code to improve performance or readability

Key Takeaways:

  • Understanding the fundamental concepts is crucial for advanced topics
  • Always consider edge cases and error handling in production code
  • Practice with real-world examples to solidify your knowledge

lessons.title: Lesson 2: Variables & Data Types
lessons.html:
PHP Variables

Variables start with $. PHP is loosely typed - no need to declare type.

Types:

TypeExample
String$name = "John"
Integer$age = 25
Float$price = 19.99
Boolean$active = true
Array$fruits = ["apple", "banana"]
<?php
$name = "Alice";
$age = 25;
$height = 1.65;
$isStudent = true;

echo "Name: $name, Age: $age, Height: $height";
if ($isStudent) {
    echo " - Student";
}
?>

lessons.title: Lesson 3: Forms & $_POST/$_GET
lessons.html:
Handling Forms

PHP receives data from HTML forms via $_POST and $_GET.

<form method="POST" action="process.php">
  Name: <input type="text" name="username"><br>
  Email: <input type="email" name="email"><br>
  <input type="submit" value="Send">
</form>
<?php  // process.php
if ($_POST) {
    $username = $_POST["username"];
    $email = $_POST["email"];
    
    echo "<h2>Welcome, $username!</h2>";
    echo "Your email: $email";
}
?>

Security: Always validate and sanitize input!

lessons.title: Lesson 4: MySQL Connection
lessons.html:
Connecting to MySQL

PHP + MySQL = dynamic websites. Use PDO for modern database connections.

<?php
// Database config
$host = "localhost";
$dbname = "myDB";
$username = "root";
$password = "";

try {
    $pdo = new PDO("mysql:host=$host;dbname=$dbname", $username, $password);
    $pdo->setAttribute(PDO::ATTR_ERRMODE, PDO::ERRMODE_EXCEPTION);
    echo "Connected successfully";
} catch(PDOException $e) {
    echo "Connection failed: " . $e->getMessage();
}
?>

Create (INSERT):

lessons.title: Lesson 6: PHP Sessions & Cookies
lessons.html:
Managing User Sessions

Sessions maintain user state across requests. Cookies store small data on the client.

Session Management:

<?php
session_start(); // Start or resume session

// Store data in session
$_SESSION['user_id'] = $user['id'];
$_SESSION['cart'] = [
    ['product_id' => 1, 'quantity' => 2],
    ['product_id' => 3, 'quantity' => 1],
];
$_SESSION['last_activity'] = time();

// Access session data
if (isset($_SESSION['user_id'])) {
    $userId = $_SESSION['user_id'];
    echo "Welcome back! Your ID: $userId";
}

// Destroy session on logout
session_destroy();
setcookie(session_name(), '', time() - 3600, '/');

Cookies:

<?php
// Set cookie (expires in 7 days)
setcookie('theme', 'dark', time() + 7 * 24 * 3600, '/');
setcookie('language', 'en', time() + 365 * 24 * 3600, '/');

// Read cookies
$theme = $_COOKIE['theme'] ?? 'light';
echo "Current theme: $theme";

// Secure cookie flags
setcookie('token', $token, [
    'expires' => time() + 3600,
    'path' => '/',
    'secure' => true,   // HTTPS only
    'httponly' => true, // Not accessible via JavaScript
    'samesite' => 'Strict', // CSRF protection
]);

Practice Exercises:

  1. Build a login system with session management
  2. Create a persistent shopping cart using sessions
  3. Implement a theme toggle using cookies

Key Takeaways:

  • Sessions store data server-side with a client cookie ID
  • session_start() must be called before any output
  • Use httponly and secure flags for production

lessons.title: Lesson 7: File Uploads & Handling
lessons.html:
Uploading Files with PHP

PHP handles file uploads through $_FILES superglobal. Always validate and secure file uploads.

Upload Form:

<form method="POST" enctype="multipart/form-data">
    <input type="file" name="avatar" accept="image/*">
    <input type="submit" value="Upload">
</form>
<?php
if ($_SERVER['REQUEST_METHOD'] === 'POST' && isset($_FILES['avatar'])) {
    $file = $_FILES['avatar'];

    // Validation
    $allowedTypes = ['image/jpeg', 'image/png', 'image/gif'];
    $maxSize = 2 * 1024 * 1024; // 2MB

    if ($file['error'] !== UPLOAD_ERR_OK) {
        die("Upload failed with error code: " . $file['error']);
    }

    if (!in_array($file['type'], $allowedTypes)) {
        die("Invalid file type. Only JPG, PNG, GIF allowed.");
    }

    if ($file['size'] > $maxSize) {
        die("File too large. Maximum size: 2MB");
    }

    // Secure filename
    $extension = pathinfo($file['name'], PATHINFO_EXTENSION);
    $newFilename = uniqid('avatar_') . '.' . $extension;
    $uploadPath = 'uploads/' . $newFilename;

    if (move_uploaded_file($file['tmp_name'], $uploadPath)) {
        echo "File uploaded successfully: $newFilename";
    } else {
        echo "Error moving uploaded file";
    }
}

Practice Exercises:

  1. Create a profile picture upload with thumbnail generation
  2. Implement multiple file upload with progress tracking
  3. Add file type validation using finfo for MIME detection

Key Takeaways:

  • Always validate file type and size server-side
  • Use uniqid() to prevent filename collisions
  • Store files outside web root for sensitive data

lessons.title: Lesson 8: Password Hashing & Security
lessons.html:
Secure Password Storage

Never store passwords in plain text. PHP provides bcrypt hashing with built-in functions.

Registration:

<?php
// Registration - hash password
$password = $_POST['password'];
$hashedPassword = password_hash($password, PASSWORD_BCRYPT, [
    'cost' => 12  // Higher cost = slower but more secure
]);

// Store in database
$stmt = $pdo->prepare("INSERT INTO users (name, email, password) VALUES (?, ?, ?)");
$stmt->execute([$_POST['name'], $_POST['email'], $hashedPassword]);

// Login - verify password
$stmt = $pdo->prepare("SELECT * FROM users WHERE email = ?");
$stmt->execute([$_POST['email']]);
$user = $stmt->fetch();

if ($user && password_verify($_POST['password'], $user['password'])) {
    $_SESSION['user_id'] = $user['id'];
    echo "Login successful!";
} else {
    echo "Invalid email or password";
}

Security Best Practices:

<?php
// CSRF Protection
token: <input type="hidden" name="csrf_token" value="<?= $_SESSION['csrf_token'] ?>">

if (!hash_equals($_SESSION['csrf_token'], $_POST['csrf_token'])) {
    die("CSRF token validation failed");
}

// SQL Injection Prevention - always use prepared statements!
// BAD: $result = $pdo->query("SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = $_GET[id]");
// GOOD:
$stmt = $pdo->prepare("SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = ?");
$stmt->execute([$_GET['id']]);

// XSS Prevention - escape output
echo htmlspecialchars($user['name'], ENT_QUOTES, 'UTF-8');

Practice Exercises:

  1. Build a complete registration and login system
  2. Add CSRF protection to all forms
  3. Implement password reset functionality

Key Takeaways:

  • password_hash() automatically generates a secure salt
  • password_verify() is timing-attack safe
  • Always escape output with htmlspecialchars()

lessons.title: Lesson 9: PHP & AJAX
lessons.html:
Asynchronous Requests with PHP

AJAX sends requests without page reload. PHP handles them and returns JSON.

PHP Endpoint:

<?php
// api/search_users.php
header('Content-Type: application/json');

if (!isset($_GET['q'])) {
    http_response_code(400);
    echo json_encode(['error' => 'Query parameter q is required']);
    exit;
}

$searchTerm = '%' . $_GET['q'] . '%';

$stmt = $pdo->prepare("SELECT id, name, email, avatar_url FROM users WHERE name LIKE ? OR email LIKE ? LIMIT 10");
$stmt->execute([$searchTerm, $searchTerm]);
$users = $stmt->fetchAll(PDO::FETCH_ASSOC);

echo json_encode([
    'status' => 'success',
    'count' => count($users),
    'data' => $users
]);

Client-Side JavaScript:

<script>
const searchInput = document.getElementById('search');
const resultsDiv = document.getElementById('results');

searchInput.addEventListener('input', async () => {
    const query = searchInput.value.trim();

    if (query.length < 2) {
        resultsDiv.innerHTML = '';
        return;
    }

    try {
        const response = await fetch(`api/search_users.php?q=${encodeURIComponent(query)}`);
        const data = await response.json();

        if (data.status === 'success') {
            resultsDiv.innerHTML = data.data.map(user => `
                <div class="user-card">
                    <img src="${user.avatar_url}" alt="${user.name}">
                    <h4>${user.name}</h4>
                    <p>${user.email}</p>
                </div>
            `).join('');
        }
    } catch (error) {
        console.error('Search failed:', error);
    }
});
</script>

Practice Exercises:

  1. Build a live search with typeahead suggestions
  2. Create an infinite scroll pagination system
  3. Implement a real-time form validation with AJAX

Key Takeaways:

  • AJAX enables partial page updates
  • PHP returns JSON for API endpoints
  • Client-side JS handles the async response

lessons.title: Lesson 10: Mini CMS Project
lessons.html:
Build a Content Management System

Combine all skills: PHP + MySQL + Sessions + File uploads into a complete CMS.

Database Schema:

CREATE TABLE users (
    id INT AUTO_INCREMENT PRIMARY KEY,
    name VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL,
    email VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL UNIQUE,
    password VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
    role ENUM('admin', 'author') DEFAULT 'author',
    created_at TIMESTAMP DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
);

CREATE TABLE posts (
    id INT AUTO_INCREMENT PRIMARY KEY,
    title VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
    content TEXT NOT NULL,
    image_url VARCHAR(500),
    author_id INT NOT NULL,
    status ENUM('draft', 'published') DEFAULT 'draft',
    created_at TIMESTAMP DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
    updated_at TIMESTAMP DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP ON UPDATE CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
    FOREIGN KEY (author_id) REFERENCES users(id)
);

Admin Dashboard:

<?php
// admin/posts.php
require_once '../includes/auth.php';
require_once '../includes/db.php';

$page = $_GET['page'] ?? 1;
$perPage = 10;
$offset = ($page - 1) * $perPage;

$stmt = $pdo->prepare("SELECT p.*, u.name AS author_name 
    FROM posts p JOIN users u ON p.author_id = u.id 
    ORDER BY p.created_at DESC LIMIT ? OFFSET ?");
$stmt->execute([$perPage, $offset]);
$posts = $stmt->fetchAll();

$countStmt = $pdo->query("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM posts");
$totalPosts = $countStmt->fetchColumn();
$totalPages = ceil($totalPosts / $perPage);
?>

<div class="admin-panel">
    <h1>Manage Posts</h1>
    <a href="create_post.php" class="btn">Create New Post</a>

    <table>
        <tr><th>Title</th><th>Author</th><th>Status</th><th>Date</th><th>Actions</th></tr>
        <?php foreach ($posts as $post): ?>
        <tr>
            <td><?= htmlspecialchars($post['title']) ?></td>
            <td><?= htmlspecialchars($post['author_name']) ?></td>
            <td><?= $post['status'] ?></td>
            <td><?= $post['created_at'] ?></td>
            <td>
                <a href="edit_post.php?id=<?= $post['id'] ?>">Edit</a>
                <a href="delete_post.php?id=<?= $post['id'] ?>" onclick="return confirm('Are you sure?')">Delete</a>
            </td>
        </tr>
        <?php endforeach; ?>
    </table>

    <?php if ($totalPages > 1): ?>
    <div class="pagination">
        <?php for ($i = 1; $i <= $totalPages; $i++): ?>
            <a href="?page=<?= $i ?>" class="<?= $i == $page ? 'active' : '' ?>"><?= $i ?></a>
        <?php endfor; ?>
    </div>
    <?php endif; ?>
</div>

Practice Exercises:

  1. Add image upload with resizing for blog posts
  2. Implement comment system with moderation
  3. Create a public-facing blog section with pagination

Key Takeaways:

  • Full-stack PHP project combines all learned skills
  • Admin panel requires authentication
  • Pagination handles large datasets
